concepts.title: Traditional Notions of Security
concepts.definition: Traditional security centres the state and external military threats: greatest danger is war and violence from other states, and responses run through balance of power and alliance building, with deterrence and defense as the chief policy instruments including nuclear deterrence.
concepts.key_idea: Security here means protecting the state - sovereignty, territory and population - from foreign military force.

solution_steps.explain: the state with its territory and sovereignty is what is secured
alliances, balance of power, deterrence and defence are the tools
nuclear deterrence rested on mutually assured destruction

concepts.title: Non-traditional Notions of Security
concepts.definition: Non-traditional security widens the referent to people and humanity: human security covers terrorism, human rights, global poverty and epidemics; global security addresses climate change, international terrorism and health epidemics that cross borders and threaten individuals more than armies do.
concepts.key_idea: When threats come from germs, warming or terror networks, armies are the wrong instrument and people, not just states, are the protected.
concepts.textbook_ref: leps105.txt human security, global poverty, epidemics and climate sections

solution_steps.explain: the referent shifts from state territory to human lives
poverty, epidemics, terrorism and climate change cross borders
no single state can arrest pandemics or warming alone

concepts.title: New Sources: Terrorism and Human Rights
concepts.definition: New threats include international terrorism by non-state networks, human rights abuses within states that the world may judge, and migration pressures; debates ask when the international community may act inside a sovereign state for humanitarian protection.
concepts.key_idea: Terror networks and rights abuses challenge both sovereignty's shield and the state's monopoly over security talk.

solution_steps.explain: terror networks operate across borders without state flags
genocide and abuse invite international scrutiny despite sovereignty

concepts.title: Cooperative Security and India's Strategy
concepts.definition: Non-traditional threats demand cooperative security - joint action through institutions and agreements rather than force; India's security strategy combines strengthening military capabilities, internal security against separatism and terrorism, and developing the economy so that no citizen feels excluded.
concepts.key_idea: India's three-pillar strategy - strength, internal stability and development - shows security as capability plus inclusion.

solution_steps.explain: treaties, forums and agreements replace unilateral force for shared threats
